name: work ARs are looked for at the recording level
why: The bug itself. _findWorkArDts() descends into the 'recording of:' <dd>; pointed at the bare div.ars instead it re-finds the RECORDING's own <dt>s, which every existing handler already claims — so the work columns vanish and the page looks exactly as it did before the feature.
grep: adds one column per work relationship

name: the work <dd> is searched at any depth
why: `:scope > dl.ars > dt` keeps a future third nesting level (a work's work's relationships, e.g. the ARs of a work reached through 'is based on:') out of this level's columns. Dropping the scope would fold them in unlabelled. KNOWN GAP, honestly recorded: MusicBrainz renders only two levels today, so no committed fixture — and nothing on the live page — has a third one for the unscoped query to reach. The guard is prophylactic, and this mutation says so rather than pretending the spec covers it.
grep: adds one column per work relationship

name: a multi-role phrase is not split
why: Seven tracks say 'lyricist and composer:' in one <dt> and the eighth states the two roles separately. Unsplit, the release carries THREE columns — 'Work lyricist and composer' (7 rows), 'Work lyricist' (1) and 'Work composer' (1) — instead of two full ones. This is the org file's explicit request.
grep: lines up with tracks crediting them separately

name: the work namespace prefix is dropped
why: Without it a work 'arranger:' and a recording 'arranger:' bucket to one key and mint one column name, where the header dedup guard silently drops the second — two relationship levels sharing a column, or one of them lost. The counter-guard test is what notices the unprefixed names appearing.
grep: work <dt>s do not leak into them

name: only the first <dt> of a role is rendered
why: 'is based on:' renders as three sibling <dt>s on Thunder Road. Taking one shows a single work and looks completely healthy — the exact bug already fixed twice, for _findPhonographicCopyrightDts and _findRecordedAtDt.

name: the entity-kind split is skipped
why: 'publisher:' credits an artist on one <dl> and labels on a sibling <dl>. Merged, one column holds Bruce Springsteen and Intersong Music Ltd. together, and the reader cannot tell which kind of publisher is which.

name: the columns land after the people-credit block
why: Placement was half of what the org asked for: the work columns read after the recording's own 'Recorded …' columns and before Performer/Vocals/Instruments. Moving the block past the CREDIT_ROLES insertions puts them at the far right, beside the dynamic-fallback columns.
grep: adds one column per work relationship

name: the header glyph is not registered
why: Org item 3: the entity glyph shown before each name on the native page has to reach the column header too. The registration is runtime-only, because these column names are not known at authoring time and so cannot be static _initColHeaderGlyph() calls.

name: collapsableColumns registration is skipped
why: initCollapsableColumns() matches by exact header string only, so a runtime-discovered column gets no per-cell ▶N▤ toggle unless it is pushed onto features.collapsableColumns here — and the three-row 'Work is based on' cell is exactly the kind that needs one.

edits.replace: // Recorded separately from the glyph array because

name: the extracted-column header tint is not applied
why: _workArColumnNames exists because the glyph array records only a column that RESOLVED a glyph, and 'is this an extracted column' is a different question from 'does it have an entity icon'. KNOWN GAP, and it corrected my own reasoning while writing this: every work relationship on this release credits an artist, a label or a work, so all seven columns are in the glyph array too and the two lists are identical here — the mutation is invisible. Observing it needs a work <dd> carrying no entity marker at all, which is _buildKindSplitListTd()'s own `kinds.size === 0` branch, already flagged there as not seen in real data.

name: the setting is ignored
why: Org item 4. Reading it as `=== true` rather than `!== false` would also break the default-on contract, but this inverts the gate outright so the off state still builds every column.

name: the row loop's no-op early return ignores the work columns
why: That guard returns before any <td> is appended when a table gained no new columns. Without _workColumnThs in it, a table whose ONLY new columns are work ones keeps its <th>s while every row is short — the column/​row mismatch this whole function is careful about. KNOWN GAP: this fixture's release also gains Recording-of/Vocals/CREDIT_ROLES columns, so the guard never fires and no committed fixture can reach it.
grep: adds one column per work relationship
